checks: Native viewport keeps a usable browser column and a start hero or restored project
Open project keeps a usable editor area at the native viewport
Native WebKit pointer input creates a committed MIDI note
Native multi-track/time-map editing shares undo and redo
Native transport reaches real FluidSynth/Pulse callbacks and stops
Native audition renders off-timeline without changing the project
Native export opens the real system save dialog and cancel unblocks it
Native binary exports and re-imports the MIDI round trip
Native import opens the real system open dialog and cancel skips import
Actual Wails window close is cancelled and preserves blank music input
Actual close/reopen preserves music and offers input without applying it
Explicit native input recovery restores the original blank value
SIGKILL/restart queries the original committed operation without replay
limits: Test build adds Wails MCP automation; production build has no automation listener
DOM input is injected by Wails automation; no claim of manual listening or physical latency

GTK4 GtkFileDialog always routes through xdg-desktop-portal; on KDE the chooser is a Qt window evidenced via KWin scripting and cancelled with closeWindow. Typing a filename into the Wayland-native dialog is not automatable here; the MIDI round trip uses explicit service paths
SIGKILL is process failure, not system power loss

Cosmetic UI state in localStorage (lastProject, view, theme) may go stale across the native quit because the WebKit storage flush is not guaranteed; music data and input drafts are durable in Go and unaffected

Audio callbacks run on the user PipeWire server routed to a temporary null sink (icetudio_p2_sink, unloaded after the run); the 2026-10-18 fully isolated secondary server could not be reproduced on the current system and no user-facing device is stopped
